results.mutant: due today counted overdue (<= instead of <)
plain `due_date: date | None` field, no pattern or validator
pattern kept, validator does not check the calendar date
today_utc frozen to a constant date
overdue list in descending id order
overdue key first in the response
list endpoints read the clock once per todo

mutation_check.note: The frozen-clock mutant passes pytest by design, because pytest patches today_utc; the live boundary/listing/overdue-list checks catch it. The clock-read-per-todo mutant is caught only by the pytest clock-read tests, since its results are equal unless midnight falls inside one request.

test_concerns.concern: None. They are unedited and pass at every commit.

The grader found that this test, from the previous revision, passed on base_sha and so proved nothing. It was removed, and its intent (overdue is never stored) became an assertion in test_overdue_flips_when_the_date_advances_without_a_write: `"overdue" not in vars(store.get(id))` after the flip. Measured now: all 34 tests in tests/test_overdue.py fail against app/ from base_sha (red_green_evidence.base_sha).

residual_uncertainty: spec.md was uploaded empty (0 bytes), so spec.json was the sole contract. No criteria conflicted, so no blocked.md was written.
Slice 1 is 368 added lines, above the 100-200 guideline. The reason is in slices[0].size_note: no smaller commit can pass the full test plan.

Slices 2 and 3 each contain tests that were already green against their parent, because their behaviour arrived in slice 1. Their red evidence is against base_sha (all 34 fail) and the mutation runs. Each slice still has at least two tests that were red against its parent.

Preview entries were not run against a deployed preview (preview.json status 'unavailable'). They were run locally against the manifest entrypoint as supplementary evidence only; the orchestrator's run is authoritative.

The live boundary/listing/overdue-list checks take 'today' from the client's UTC clock, so they assume the client and the service share a clock (true when the orchestrator runs them on the same host). They retry if the UTC date changes mid-check.
On a shared instance, compat cannot assert id == 1, because ids depend on prior todos. It asserts the new id is above every id listed before the POST; pytest asserts id == 1 on an empty store.

Concurrency: list_dicts builds the response dicts while holding the store lock, which complete() also takes, so within one list response done and overdue come from one snapshot. No deterministic test covers this race. The POST routes call to_dict() outside the lock, as the spec prescribes.
The platform-contract skill was not available in this sandbox. Per the spec context no env var, port, migration or manifest change was needed, and service_manifest.json is unchanged.
